concepts.def: y = aˣ with a > 0, a ≠ 1. Grows rapidly if a > 1; decays if 0 < a < 1. Always passes through (0, 1).
y = eˣ where e ≈ 2.71828. Unique property: d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ. Used for continuous growth/decay.
logₐ x is the inverse of aˣ: logₐ x = y ⟺ aʸ = x. Natural log: ln x = logₑ x.
log(xy) = log x + log y; log(x/y) = log x − log y; log(xⁿ) = n log x. Same base throughout.
logₐ x = logᵦ x / logᵦ a. Useful when calculator only has log₁₀ or ln.
Population growth, radioactive decay, Newton's law of cooling: all use y = Aeᵏᵗ. Log transforms linearise data.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Exponentials & Logarithms — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Exponentials & Logarithms brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Exponentials & Logarithms.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Yes — if the function is below the x-axis over the interval, the integral is negative.
Definite integrals are negative only when the limits are reversed.
Definite integrals are always positive because area cannot be negative.

mcqs.q: In Pythagoras' theorem, which side does c^2 represent?
options: c^2 represents the side opposite the largest angle that is not 90 degrees.
c^2 represents any side of the triangle as long as the other two are squared.
The hypotenuse — the longest side, opposite the right angle.
1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.
